headline: Town boards prepared for Special Town Meeting warrant debates while school officials advanced a $38 million Neary Elementary renovation plan.
synopsis: Heading into the October Special Town Meeting, municipal boards staked out contrasting positions on high-profile warrant articles, including Community Preservation Act funding for the Peninsula Trail footbridge and golf course irrigation. The Elementary School Building Committee pivoted toward a $38 million addition and renovation plan for Neary Elementary after architect analysis revealed a $15 million baseline upgrade would be consumed by code-mandated fire and accessibility work. Meanwhile, the school district reported the Neary roof replacement is 90 percent complete and will return nearly $2 million in unspent borrowing authorization to the town. School officials also approved an amended teacher contract aligning local educator salaries with Algonquin Regional High School by 2027. Regional school subcommittees reported an impending $800,000 net drop in regional debt service after fiscal year 2027 alongside potential health insurance savings.

top_items.title: Neary School Building Project Weighs $38 Million Option
top_items.why: Architect analysis revealed a $15 million upgrade leaves only $5.8 million for direct construction after accounting for soft costs and code-required fire and accessibility upgrades. As a result, the Elementary School Building Committee focused on advancing a $38 million addition and renovation plan.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects presented detailed cost comparisons showing that a $15 million baseline repair package for Margaret A. Neary Elementary School would be largely consumed by mandatory fire sprinkler systems and Americans with Disabilities Act renovations triggered by building code thresholds. The baseline option would leave boilers, unit ventilators, flooring, and educational upgrades unaddressed and would not qualify for state Massachusetts School Building Authority reimbursement. The building committee directed architects to proceed with schematic design drawings and renderings for Option 3, a comprehensive $38 million addition and renovation, while the School Committee plans to consider whether to submit a new Statement of Interest to the MSBA in November.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail Footbridge Moves to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance Article 4 requesting $217,318 in additional CPA funding for a pedestrian bridge without reductions. The proposal faces formal opposition from both the Select Board and the Advisory Committee over project costs.
top_items.body: Warrant Article 4 seeks to bring total Community Preservation Act funding for the 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian footbridge along Route 30 to $428,550. Despite earlier discussions within the Trails Committee about a potential floor amendment to scale back the ask, the Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee decided to put the full appropriation before voters as printed. The Advisory Committee unanimously recommended against approval, expressing concern over an estimated cost of roughly $5,000 per linear foot for the bridge structure.

top_items.title: Debate Over CPA Funding for Golf Course Irrigation
top_items.why: Town boards remain divided over Article 3, which requests $433,546 in CPA funds and $100,000 from the golf revolving fund for an estimated $1 million irrigation system overhaul.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee finalized report text opposing the use of Community Preservation Act funds for the Southborough Golf Club irrigation system, arguing the municipal course was intended to be self-sustaining through player fees rather than taxpayer-backed CPA grants. The Golf Committee and Community Preservation Committee endorsed the measure, preparing informational handouts and confirming that $553,750 in previously approved CPA funds will expire in December if the project is not advanced. In a related action, the Golf Committee voted to allocate up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to cover a consultant shortfall for its Audubon International certification.

top_items.title: Two-Family Zoning Amendment Heads to Voters
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to support Warrant Article 2 as drafted, while the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation.
top_items.body: The proposed zoning bylaw amendment would eliminate the two-year ownership waiting period before converting single-family dwellings into two-family homes. While the ZBA and Select Board endorsed the article as written to create housing flexibility, the Advisory Committee recommended defeat. Advisory members cited potential risks of speculative property flipping, neighborhood density increases, and concerns that relying on standard percolation tests could compromise septic capacity.

top_items.title: Water Line Extension for Homes Near Parkerville Landfill
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend approving $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the closed Parkerville Road landfill to municipal water.
top_items.body: Article 7 at Special Town Meeting would extend a water main to supply two residential properties where groundwater contamination testing has been conducted near the town landfill. Under the plan, the town will cover the service connections from the street directly into the homes. The measure has unanimous backing from both the Select Board and Advisory Committee to resolve environmental health concerns and avoid ongoing state-mandated private well testing costs.

top_items.title: Teacher Contract Amended to Align with Algonquin
top_items.why: The School Committee unanimously approved contract changes for Southborough Teachers Association Unit A to align the local salary schedule with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027.
top_items.body: The School Committee approved amendments to Articles 22 and 29 of the Unit A collective bargaining agreement, revising the teacher retirement incentive program and aligning Southborough's salary scales with the regional high school. Administration also presented the FY27 first-quarter budget report, which maintains a $349,347 available balance after absorbing the cost of two additional elementary teachers hired over the summer, and confirmed that the Neary School roof project is nearly 90 percent complete with approximately $2 million in borrowing expected to be returned.

top_items.title: Regional School District Anticipates Debt Service Drop
top_items.why: Regional school subcommittees reported an estimated $800,000 net reduction in high school debt service following FY27 as original 2004 renovation bonds expire.
top_items.body: Operational Budget and Capital Planning subcommittees reviewed early FY28 regional budget parameters, highlighting that the expiration of long-term debt from the 2004 Algonquin renovation will produce an $800,000 net drop in regional debt service, even with borrowing for the athletic complex factored in. Administration is also preparing to restructure employee health insurance deductibles to mirror state Group Insurance Commission levels, projecting roughly $600,000 in regional savings. In response to tight revenue environments under Proposition 2 1/2 in Southborough and Northborough, administrators will model level-service, 3% capped, and flat-funded budgets for FY28.
